newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms develop protocol for digital camera.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms develop protocol for digital camera.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and four other Japanese companies said on Monday they had jointly developed a protocol for exchanging digital image data between digital still cameras and other consumer electronics devices made by different manufacturers.
The four other companies are Casio Computer Co Ltd, Sharp Corp, Sony Corp and Okaya Systemware Co Ltd.

The new protocol, called IrTran-P, makes it possible to transfer data from a digital camera of one manufacturer which uses an infrared data communication interface to other digital cameras, video printers, digital video recorders and personal computers (PCs) made by different companies which also use infrared data communication interfaces, they said in a statement.
Infared data communication is a form of wireless communication between PCs and peripherals.
The five companies will provide information on the new protocol to other manufacturers so that they will also be able to use the protocol, an NTT official said.

"To make the IrTran-P an open standard, the five companies will propose the protocol to the general meeting of the Infrared Data Association this July at Portland, Oregon," the five companies said in the statement.

Casio, Sharp and Sony will work to develop commercial products which utilise the new protocol-based communication module, while Okaya will develop and supply IrTran-P-based software modules which can be used in PCs and personal digital assistants, they said.
